events.title: Battle of Gravelines Concludes
events.description: The English fleet defeated the Spanish Armada off the coast of Gravelines, France, on 8 August 1588 (Gregorian calendar). The battle ended in a decisive English victory and the scattering of the Spanish fleet, which was forced to flee north around Scotland and Ireland, where many ships were wrecked in storms.
events.significance: The failure of the Armada ended Spain's invasion plans against England, strengthened Elizabeth I's reign and English naval power, and is seen as a turning point in the rise of England as a maritime power.

events.title: Soviet Union Declares War on Japan
events.description: On 8 August 1945, two days after the atomic bombing of Hiroshima and one day before Nagasaki, the Soviet Union declared war on Japan, and launched the invasion of Japanese-held Manchuria shortly after midnight.
events.significance: The Soviet entry into the Pacific War, together with the atomic bombings, added to the pressure on Japan to surrender, which was announced on 15 August 1945, and shaped postwar territorial arrangements in East Asia.

events.title: Nixon Announces Resignation
events.description: In a televised address on the evening of 8 August 1974, U.S. President Richard Nixon announced that he would resign the presidency effective at noon the next day, in the face of near-certain impeachment over the Watergate scandal.
events.significance: Nixon became the only U.S. president to resign from office. Gerald Ford succeeded him, and the episode reshaped American public trust in government and strengthened scrutiny of executive power.

events.title: Opening of the Beijing Summer Olympics
events.description: The Games of the XXIX Olympiad opened on 8 August 2008 (8/8/08, an auspicious date in Chinese culture) at the Beijing National Stadium, known as the Bird's Nest, with a lavish ceremony directed by Zhang Yimou.
events.significance: The Games marked China's emergence as a major global power on the world stage, and Michael Phelps went on to win a record eight gold medals at a single Games. The opening day also coincided with the start of the Russo-Georgian War.

events.title: Great Train Robbery
events.description: On 8 August 1963, a gang of 15 men held up a Royal Mail train traveling from Glasgow to London at Bridego Railway Bridge in Buckinghamshire, England, stealing about £2.6 million in cash.
events.significance: One of the most famous heists in history, it led to a massive police investigation, lengthy prison sentences for the participants, and became a lasting part of British popular culture.
